title: Construction of Defined Human Engineered Cardiac Tissues to Study Mechanisms of Cardiac Cell Therapy
protocol: Thaw 150 µl aliquot of hESC qualified basement membrane matrix on ice overnight at 4 °C.
Dilute the thawed matrix into 12 ml of ice-cold DMEM/F12 and mix well.
Transfer 1 ml of the DMEM/F12-matrix solution into each well of a 6-well tissue culture treated dish.
Incubate the coated plates at room temperature for at least 1 hr.
At approximately 75% confluence, dissociate the H7 hESCs from the 10 cm dish using 6 ml of the non-enzymatic dissociation reagent.
After 5 min, gently scrape the cells from the culture surface using a disposable cell scraper and transfer the cell suspension to a sterile 15 ml centrifuge tube.
Remove 0.5 ml of the dissociation solution with cells from the 15 ml tube.
Transfer the 0.5 ml of cells to a new sterile 15 ml tube.
Pellet the 0.5 ml of cells at 300 x g for 5 min at 20 °C.
Remove the supernatant from the pelleted cells.
Gently resuspend the pellet in 8 ml of pluripotent stem cell media containing 1% penicillin-streptomycin.
Transfer the resuspended cells to a new, coated, 10 cm tissue culture dish.
Maintain the stem cell line at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Add 5.5 µl of 10 mM ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 to the remaining 5.5 ml of dissociation solution.
Incubate the solution with the inhibitor at room temperature for another 5-10 min.
Gently mix the cells in the solution with a 5 ml serological pipet.
Continue incubating until a single cell suspension is achieved.
Pellet the cells at 300 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Resuspend the cells in 5 ml of pluripotent stem cell media.
Perform a cell count using a hemocytometer.
Seed each well of the 6-well dish with 140,000 cells per well.
Seed two 6-well plates to create six defined tissues.
Dispose of any remaining cells after plating.
Fill each well to 1 ml with pluripotent stem cell media.
Incubate at 37 °C and 5% CO2.
Remove the media from the wells twenty-four hours later.
Add 2 ml of fresh pluripotent stem cell media to each well.
Check the confluence of the plates each day.
Begin differentiation once cells reach approximately 75% confluence.
Prepare RPMI differentiation media I by combining 500 ml RPMI 1640 with 10 ml B27 supplement (without insulin) and 5 ml penicillin-streptomycin stock solution.
Aliquot the prepared media into 50 ml tubes on ice and store at 4°C.
Prepare mesoderm induction media by adding 2.4 µl of CHIR99021 (10 mM stock, 6 µM final concentration) to 12 ml RPMI differentiation media I.
Remove pluripotent stem cell media from each well.
Replace with 2 ml of mesoderm induction media per well.
Return the plate to the incubator.
Rinse dead cells away with DMEM/F12 rinse if significant cell death occurs.
Prepare fresh mesoderm induction media as described previously.
Remove old media from each well on Day 5 (Differentiation Day 1).
Rinse once with 1 ml of DMEM/F12 per well.
Add 2 ml of fresh mesoderm induction media to each well.
Remove cardiac induction media.
Rinse once with 1 ml DMEM/F12 per well.
Replace rinse with 2 ml RPMI differentiation media I and return to the incubator.
Prepare cardiac mesoderm induction media by adding 6 µl of the small molecule Wnt inhibitor IWR-1 (5 µM final) to 12 ml of RPMI differentiation media I.
Remove media from each well.
Rinse once with 1 ml DMEM/F12 per well.
Replace with 2 ml cardiac mesoderm induction media per well and return to the incubator.
Prepare an additional 12 ml of cardiac mesoderm induction media as described above.
Remove media added the day prior.
Rinse once with 1 ml DMEM/F12 per well.
Replace with 2 ml fresh cardiac mesoderm differentiation media per well and return to the incubator.
On both days, remove cardiac mesoderm induction media.
Rinse each well with 1 ml of DMEM/F12.
Add 2 ml of fresh RPMI differentiation media I (no small molecules added but still with B27 supplement) to each well and return plate to the incubator.
Prepare RPMI differentiation media II by combining 500 ml RPMI 1640 with 10 ml B27 supplement and 5 ml penicillin-streptomycin stock solution.
Aliquot the prepared differentiation media into 50 ml tubes on ice.
Store the aliquoted differentiation media at 4 °C.
Remove RPMI differentiation media without insulin from each well.
Rinse each well with 1 ml DMEM/F12.
Replace the rinse with 2 ml of RPMI differentiation media II containing insulin.
Return the wells to the incubator.
Monitor spontaneous beating between days 7 and 10; if no beating is observed by day 15, start a new differentiation protocol.
Remove old differentiation media daily from each well starting on day 8.
Replace with 2 ml fresh RPMI differentiation media II per well for cell maturation and organization of the beating monolayer.
Rinse once with 1 ml PBS to remove differentiation media.
Dissociate the monolayers by adding 1 ml enzymatic dissociation solution (0.04% Trypsin/0.03% EDTA) to each well.
Move plate into incubator for 10 min.
Add 12 μl of ROCK inhibitor to 6 ml of trypsin neutralization solution.
Gently add 1 ml of the trypsin neutralization solution containing the ROCK inhibitor to each well of the plate.
Using a sterile transfer pipet, gently mix each well to break apart the cell clusters.
Transfer all 12 ml from the 6-well plate to a 15 ml centrifuge tube.
Transfer 3 ml of PBS to one well of the plate and sequentially to each subsequent well.
Transfer the remaining 3 ml from the final well into the same 15 ml centrifuge tube containing the cells.
Pellet at 300 x g for 5 min at 4 °C.
Prepare staining buffer by adding 5 ml of Fetal Bovine Serum to 45 ml of PBS on ice with 50 μl of ROCK inhibitor.
Remove supernatant from the cell pellet and resuspend in 1.2 ml of staining buffer.
Transfer 200 μl of the cell suspension to a new, pre-chilled, 50 ml centrifuge tube on ice for negative staining control.
Transfer remaining 1 ml of cell suspension to a new, pre-chilled, 50 ml centrifuge tube on ice.
Add 2 µl SIRPα-PE/Cy7 (1:500 dilution) and 4 µl CD90-FITC (1:250 dilution) to the cell suspension.
Gently mix the cell suspension with a transfer pipet.
Incubate both the negative control and sample on a rocker shaker on ice at 4 °C for 1 hour.
Prepare sample collection tubes by adding 3 ml of RPMI media (with insulin) to two 15 ml centrifuge tubes.
Add 3 µl of ROCK inhibitor to each tube and store on ice.
Pellet the stained cells at 300 x g for 5 minutes at 4 °C.
Rinse the pellet twice with at least 10 ml of ice-cold PBS per rinse.
Add 1 µl of DAPI (1 µg/ml) to 5 ml of staining buffer.
Gently resuspend the sample pellet with 1-3 ml of the DAPI-containing staining buffer using a transfer pipet.
Add 500 µl of staining buffer (with no DAPI added) to the negative control.
Gently filter both the negative control and sample through a 40 µm cell strainer to remove clumps of cells.
Transfer the filtered samples to polystyrene FACS tubes on ice.
Immediately bring the samples to the cell sorter.
Use the negative control to set the gates, select for live cells (DAPI negative).
Collect both the FITC+ (i.e., CD90+ fibroblasts) and PE/Cy7+ (i.e., SIRPα+ cardiomyocytes) populations independently at 20 psi.
Pellet both collection tubes after cell sort.
Resuspend cells in 1 ml of DMEM containing 10% Neonatal Bovine Serum, 1% penicillin-streptomycin and 0.2% Amphotericin B.
Recombine SIRPα+ and CD90+ cells in a 3:1 ratio.
Plate combined cells at a density of 2 million cells per 60 cm² in non-tissue culture treated petri dish.
Add 10 ml of NBS media to cell suspension.
Add 10 μl of ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 to cell suspension.
Place cell suspension in the tissue culture incubator for 48 hours.
Machine a frame from polysulfone measuring 25 x 35 x 11 mm³.
Machine 6 wells (6 x 1 x 1 mm³), 4 mm apart, into a 20 x 40 x 5 mm³ piece of black polytetrafluoroethylene to form the baseplate.
Mix elastomeric base and curing agent for PDMS in a 10:1 w/w ratio.
Add the mixture to the custom polytetrafluoroethylene mold to create two rows of six force-sensing posts.
Incubate the mixture overnight at 80 °C under vacuum.
Gently remove the cured PDMS from the master mold after incubation.
Mark the tops of each post with a black permanent marker for enhanced contrast and automated real-time post deflection tracking.
Sterilize all components in a steam autoclave.
Remove the reaggregated cells from the incubator and transfer all 10 ml of the reaggregation media to a 50 ml centrifuge tube.
Rinse the plate with 3 ml of PBS and transfer the rinse to the same 50 ml centrifuge tube containing the reaggregation media.
Add 3 ml of 0.04% Trypsin/0.03% EDTA to the 10 cm dish and return to the incubator for 5 min.
Examine the plate with an inverted compound microscope at 10X magnification to ensure complete cell dissociation from the dish after 5 min.
If some residual clusters are still attached, gently agitate the plate to detach the clumps.
If the clusters remain attached, return to the incubator for another 2-3 min.
Add 3 ml of trypsin neutralization solution once all cells are detached.
Gently mix the neutralization solution with the trypsin-cell solution and transfer to the 50 ml centrifuge tube containing the reaggregation media and rinse once with PBS.
Rinse the entire dish with 5 ml of PBS and transfer to the same 50 ml tube containing the cells.
Pellet the cells at 300 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant from the cardiac cells.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 ml of NBS media.
Transfer the suspension to a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Pellet the cells at 300 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant from the pelleted cells.
(Optional) Collect supplemental cell type of interest (e.g., mesenchymal stem cells).
Use 0.25% trypsin/0.1% EDTA to collect the cells.
Pellet the collected cells at 300 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Resuspend the pelleted cells in 5 ml of appropriate cell culture media.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Pellet the cells again at 300 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant from the cells.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 ml of cell culture media.
Transfer the suspension to a 1.5 ml microcentrifuge tube.
Pellet the cells at 300 x g for 5 min at room temperature.
Remove the supernatant.
Dilute 60.0 µl of the 5 mg/ml collagen stock to 3.125 mg/ml with 1.5 µl of 1 M NaOH, 9.6 µl of 10x PBS and 24.9 µl of sterile ultrapure deionized water.
Add 12.0 µl of both 10x MEM and 0.2 N HEPES pH 9 to the dilute collagen mixture to create the collagen mix.
Add the basement membrane matrix to a final concentration of 0.9 mg/ml to the collagen mix and store on ice to create the final tissue mix.
Add 500,000 reaggregated cells to the tissue mix.
Fill to a final volume of 25 μl per tissue with either cell-free NBS media or 50,000 cells of the supplemental cell type of interest.
Mix well to form an even cell suspension.
Pipette 25 μl of the cell suspension into each of the six wells in the bioreactor baseplate.
Push two rows of the PDMS force sensors onto either side of the polysulfone frame, forming 6 pairs of opposing posts.
Invert the frame on top of the baseplate so that one pair of posts enters each well containing the cell suspension.
Place the bioreactor, baseplate down, into a 60 mm dish.
Place the dish without its cover inside of a 10 cm dish.
Place the 10 cm cover on top and move the entire bioreactor assembly into the tissue culture incubator.
Wait two hours for the tissue to gel.
Remove the bioreactor from the incubator after 2 hr.
Add 14 ml of NBS media to the entire assembly, enough to cover the baseplate.
Return the bioreactor to the incubator and change half of the media every day.
Remove the baseplate by gently moving each side a few millimeters at a time.
Change the media.
Return the bioreactor, tissues facing down, to the media.
Continue changing half of the NBS culture media every day.
